claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in HEA multilayer coatings is primarily governed by interface-barrier strengthening.
A high density of phase or orientation boundaries impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion delays plastic flow under sustained load.
Changing a coating from a homogeneous film to alternating nanoscale layers increases its interface density.
Thin-layer multilayer architecture maximizes interface density relative to a continuous homogeneous film.
Layer boundaries act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Layer boundaries promote dislocation pile-up.
Under the proposed sustained thermal and mechanical loading, dislocation motion is the primary creep mechanism.
Interfaces hinder dislocation propagation through the multilayer coating.
Interrupting dislocation flow increases the effective local stress required for further plastic deformation.
Multilayer HEA coatings will have a significantly lower creep rate than homogeneous single-layer coatings of the same average composition.
Multilayer HEA coatings will exhibit less time-dependent plastic deformation because their interfaces block dislocations.
The interface-strengthening effect is most pronounced below a critical nanoscale layer-thickness threshold.
The proposed mechanism applies in a 500–700°C regime where creep is active.
The effect may not hold at temperatures that suppress dislocation activity.
Very high temperatures may destabilize the multilayer through interdiffusion.
Compositional gradients or residual stresses may also contribute to the creep response.
A controlled comparison using the same deposition method, average composition, creep temperature, stress, and duration can test the effect of stacking architecture.
The interface-barrier hypothesis predicts enhanced post-test dislocation pile-ups at multilayer interfaces.
Failure to observe a statistically significant creep-rate reduction in the multilayer relative to the homogeneous control would falsify the stated prediction under the tested conditions.
